verdicts.reason: The Bonferroni adjustment and its interpretation are clear.
The reported p-value is inconsistent with the displayed chi-square statistic and degrees of freedom.
The reported confidence interval has a width inconsistent with the displayed t-statistic, degrees of freedom, and difference in means.
The stated planning approximation identifies one sample-size change.
The assumptions identify one property that must hold.
The data, permutation rule, tail, and rounding are specified.
The two sample summaries determine the direction of the p-value change.
The reported F-statistic is inconsistent with the displayed R-squared and degrees of freedom.
The reported two-sided Fisher exact p-value is inconsistent with the supplied contingency table.
The wording can refer to empirical quantiles of the simulated sample means or to a confidence interval for their mean based on Monte Carlo standard error.
The resampling description establishes prediction variability, but the polynomial's training fit does not establish its bias on new data.
The desired treatment of missing values is explicit.
One option gives the defining relationship between the canonical link and the natural parameter.
The displayed Shapiro–Wilk statistic and sample size are inconsistent with the reported R p-value.
The data, standard deviation convention, and rounding are specified.
The VIFs support one interpretation about the precision of coefficient estimates.
In a three-predictor regression, the two equal VIFs shown are too small to coexist with the reported VIF for the third predictor.
The fitted equation and last observation determine the requested forecast.
The seed, simulation size, success probability, and return value are specified.
The question leaves the interaction model unspecified, and with independent random interactions both the treatment and residual expected mean squares include an interaction variance component.
With tied scores, standard ROC AUC includes half the probability of a tie, which all options omit.
The complete symmetric permutation distribution and observed statistic determine the two-sided p-value.
Under the usual all-else-equal comparison, one change narrows the interval.
The option with normality and a common variance omits independent random sampling, which is also required for the standard exact derivation.
The quartile convention and rounding are explicit.
One option identifies the common data required for the stated AIC comparison.
The warning reports numerically extreme fitted probabilities, which can occur without perfect separation.
The posterior predictive variance has a standard decomposition.
The reported t-statistics and p-values for the two estimated meal-plan coefficients cannot share a single residual degrees of freedom.
The regression summaries suffice for the usual prediction interval.
The code and data determine the requested coefficient.
One option correctly distinguishes how the designs sample groups.
The coefficient has a clear conditional interpretation in the stated model.
The exponential model and supplied formula determine the requested expectation.
The test output and significance level support one conclusion.
The interaction model specifies where the coefficient equals the partial derivative.
The squared component standard deviations sum to about one, whereas PCA of three standardized variables has total variance three.
The coefficient, standard error, confidence level, and rounding are specified.
One option correctly distinguishes empirical resampling from sampling from a fitted family.
The squared component standard deviations neither sum to four nor yield the displayed variance proportions.
The placebo arm can estimate the banner's effect relative to control, but the design cannot isolate an algorithm effect stripped of psychological responses.
The R expression and requested precision are explicit.
The only plausible option states an exact chi-square null distribution for a deviance difference whose chi-square reference distribution is asymptotic.
The z-test relationship between effect size, standard error, and p-value is well defined.
The GLM family and dispersion treatment are unspecified, so the deviance difference alone does not determine the likelihood-ratio p-value.
The residual deviance exceeds the null deviance even though the fitted Poisson model contains the null model with the same offset.
R can fit the Gaussian model to numeric count data, and the response's support alone does not establish a family specification error.
The displayed 80% and 95% half-widths are inconsistent with Gaussian quantiles applied to the same forecast standard error.
The equal confidence interval widths and the displayed adjusted p-values are inconsistent with a common Tukey studentized-range reference distribution.
The adjusted values are consistent with the stated method and have one valid interpretation among the choices.
